lines: A wavetable oscillator that plays a .wav file you load, splitting it into single cycles and sweeping between them; sixteen channels of polyphony
Sweeps through the cycles of the loaded wavetable, 0 at the first cycle and 1 at the last, mixing the two nearest cycles in between
Moves the position through the wavetable, one full sweep per 10V, added to the pos knob and clamped to the ends of the table
Shifts the pitch by up to half an octave either way, added to what the V/oct knob sets
Shifts the pitch by one octave per 5V, added to what the knobs and the V/oct input set
Sets the pitch in octaves, -3 to +3 from C4 at 261.63Hz with the knob centred
Sets the pitch at 1V per octave, added to what the knobs set; the number of channels here is also the number of voices the oscillator runs
The oscillator, plus and minus 5V, with as many channels as the V/oct input carries
Note — a new module plays a single-cycle saw wave and stays on it until you load a wavetable from the right-click menu, either one of the four presets or a .wav file of your own
Note — the pitch the knobs and both pitch inputs add up to is clamped to 3.5 octaves either side of C4, about 23Hz at the bottom and about 2960Hz at the top
Note — the lamp on the panel is lit once a wavetable has been read, and stays dark while the built-in saw wave is playing
Menu — Current table — the name of the .wav file in use, with no extension, or Single Saw for the built-in wave; it cannot be clicked
Menu — Load wavetable: 256 samples/cycle, 512 samples/cycle, 1024 samples/cycle, 2048 samples/cycle — says how long one cycle of the file is, then opens a file chooser for the .wav to read
Menu — Preset wavetables: Harmonic, Chebyshev, Formant, Spectral Noise — loads one of the four wavetables that ship with the plugin, each read at 2048 samples per cycle
Note — a file is cut into at most 256 cycles; anything past that is dropped, and a file shorter than one cycle is played as a single cycle of whatever length it has

table.notes: Read from source at commit fb63bc3, the state of the tree that the installed 2.0.0 binary matches; the only later source commit, 53c691a, changes select and not this module. The maker's tooltip on the V/oct knob reads Coarse, which is what the panel calls it in the repository's own doc/table.md; the panel prints V/oct and that is the name used above. wavetable.cpp:110 writes each incoming sample to cycleBuffers[i / cycleLength][cycleLength - i % cycleLength], so every cycle is stored back to front and the sample at offset 0 lands one past the slice that is read back at line 128; the maker comments on the reversal at line 107 and treats it as a fix rather than a fault. The output is bandlimited per octave by the EarLevel WaveTableOsc code in src/dsp/osc/earlevel.

lines: A sixteen-to-one switch: a knob chooses which of sixteen input jacks reaches the output, carrying all of its polyphonic channels
One of sixteen inputs; it reaches out when the knob is set to its number, and a lamp beside it lights while it is the chosen one
Chooses which input reaches out, stepping through the numbers 0 to 15
Carries whatever is on the chosen input, with the same number of channels; it reads 0V on one channel while that input is unpatched
Note — the inputs are numbered 0 to 15, running 0 to 7 down the left column and 8 to 15 down the right, and the knob's number picks one of them
Note — nothing is mixed or summed here: the fifteen inputs that are not chosen are read nowhere, and changing the knob cuts straight from one to the other with no crossfade

select.notes: Read from source at commit fb63bc3. The installed 2.0.0 binary is that state and not the repository HEAD: the configParam in Select::Select disassembles as min 0, max 15, default 0, and Select::process converts the knob with fcvtzs and uses it as the port index with no subtraction, which is the code before commit 53c691a changed the knob to count 1 to 16 and subtract one. So the knob's tooltip in this build reads Selected: 0 to Selected: 15. The panel prints no numbers at all, on the jacks or the knob, so nothing on screen contradicts it. No family is given for any of the jacks: this is a pass-through and each carries whatever is patched into it. The sixteen inputs and the output are never named with configInput or configOutput, so Rack's own tooltips for them are empty.

lines: An eight-bit elementary cellular automaton clocked one generation at a time, with a gate output for each bit and a CV output taken from the eight bits read as a number
Sets the rule number, 0 to 255, that turns each generation into the next one; it starts at 90
Adds its voltage to the rule number, one step per volt, with the total clamped to 0 and 255; polyphonic channels are summed first
Sets the eight-bit number the run starts from, 0 to 255; it starts at 30, and moving it restarts the run
Adds its voltage to the seed number, one step per volt, with the total clamped to 0 and 255; polyphonic channels are summed first
Sets one end of the range of scale steps the quantized CV output is drawn from, 0 to 28 steps up the scale
Moves that end of the range, adding nothing at -10V and all 28 steps at 10V on top of the low knob, so a cable resting at 0V adds 14 by itself
Sets the other end of the range of scale steps, 0 to 28, and may be set below the low knob without breaking the range
Moves that end of the range, adding nothing at -10V and all 28 steps at 10V on top of the high knob, so a cable resting at 0V adds 14 by itself
Chooses the scale the quantized CV is snapped to: ionian, aeolian, dorian, phrygian, lydian, mixolydian, major pent, minor pent, shang, jiao, zhi, todi, purvi, marva, bhairav, ahirbhairav, chromatic
Moves the scale choice, adding nothing at -10V and all sixteen places at 10V on top of the scale knob, so a cable resting at 0V steps it on by eight
Chooses which of the eight bits drives the clock output and gates the CV output, 0 for the least significant bit and 7 for the most
Moves the chosen bit, adding nothing at -10V and all seven places at 10V on top of the bit knob, so a cable resting at 0V adds three and a half before the total is rounded down
Steps the automaton on to the next generation on each rising edge, reading high at 1V and low again at 0.1V
Nothing in the module reads this jack; the run is restarted only by the reset button beside it
Clears the run and works out the first generation from the seed again, which is one step on from the seed itself
Chooses what the CV output carries: at qnt a pitch snapped to the scale, at raw a plain voltage scaled to the span set on the menu; it comes up at qnt
At thru the CV output takes a new value on every clock; at sel only on a clock where the chosen bit is high. The tooltip calls this Clock output mode, but the clock output is the same either way
Carries 10V while the clock input is high and its own bit of the current generation is 1, and 0V the rest of the time
The current generation read as a number and turned into a voltage: at qnt a pitch at 1V per octave with the bottom of the scale at C3, at raw the number spread across the span set on the menu
Carries 10V while the clock input is high and the bit named by the bit knob is 1, and 0V the rest of the time
Note — nothing moves until a clock is patched to clock; the automaton takes one generation per rising edge there, and every output holds 0V while that jack is low
Note — the eight gate outputs run from bit 0 at the top to bit 7 at the bottom, bit 0 being the least significant bit of the eight-bit generation
Note — a rule of 0, or a seed of 0, gives generations that are all zero, so the gate outputs and the clock output stay at 0V however fast the clock runs
Note — the picture on the panel is worked out from the rule and the seed alone and shows 64 generations of the run at once; it is redrawn when either knob moves, not on each clock
Note — the white lamp beside each gate output shows that bit of the current generation, and the green lamp shows which bit the bit knob has chosen
Menu — Raw CV output range: +/- 10V, +/- 5V, +/- 3V, +/- 1V, 0V - 10V, 0V - 5V, 0V - 3V, 0V - 1V — sets the span the CV output covers at raw, and changes nothing at qnt

more-ideas.notes: Read from source at commit fb63bc3, the state the installed 2.0.0 binary matches: the six configParam calls in More_ideas::More_ideas disassemble to the same ranges and defaults (rule 0 to 255 starting at 90, seed 0 to 255 starting at 30, low and high 0 to 28 starting at 0 and 14, scale 0 to 16, bit 0 to 7). THE MAKER'S OWN doc/more_ideas.md DISAGREES WITH THE CODE ABOUT THE thru / sel SWITCH. It says thru passes the input clock through to the clock output and sel pulses on any change of output CV. Neither is what happens: the clock output at lines 112 and 118 is 10V whenever the clock input is high and the chosen bit of the generation is 1, whichever way the switch is set. What the switch actually decides, at line 82, is whether the CV output is rewritten on every clock or only on a clock where the chosen bit is high. The maker's tooltip for it, Clock output mode, points at the clock output for the same reason and is wrong in the same way. The CV output is tagged pitch because the module comes up quantized; at raw it carries a plain control voltage over whatever span the menu names, so the colour is right for the default and not for both settings. The reset input is declared and drawn and read nowhere, so it gets a line saying so rather than being left to show an empty tooltip. All ten outputs and the eight lamp pairs are updated in subSampledProcess, which runs once every nine samples, so the gate edges follow the clock input to within that. None of the eight inputs is named with configInput, so Rack's own tooltips for them are empty.
